strings: A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A huge chunk of metal used to separate rooms.
Your instincts say you shouldn't be following these.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
A station intercom. It looks like it has been modified to not broadcast.
A nicely-crafted wooden dresser. It's filled with lots of undies.
A structure built out of bricks, for heating up metal, or glass, or ceramic, or food, or anything really.

A compact heating and cooling device for large scale applications, made to mount onto walls up and out of the way. 		It charges with the nearest APC; the internal cell buffers the power to the heating/cooling mechanism.
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.
A crown fit for a king, a petty king maybe.
Could probably save Cargo's budget if the QM sold that damn thing. Uses .357 ammo.
A metal pole, the likes of which are commonly used as an antennae, structural support, or simply to maneuver in zero-g.
A fluctuating forcefield for ships to cross.
A basin used to grow plants in.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
Used to call and send the labor camp shuttle.

An industrial unit made to hold, charge, and decontaminate equipment. It comes with a built-in UV cauterization mechanism. A small warning label advises that organic matter should not be placed into the unit.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A luxurious double bed, for those too important for small dreams.
It is decorated with a crate emblem in silver lining.  It's rather tough, and just the thing to lie on after a hard day of pushing paper.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.

The \"Dynamic Rapid-Apprehension of the Guilty Network\" translocation shotgun (or DRAGnet for short) is a revolution in law enforcement technology. 		By syncing the weapon to a DRAGnet beacon, the bluespace transportation fields produced by the weapon's 'snare' function can rapidly exfiltrate an entire 		security squad, with criminal in tow. Otherwise, the weapon is an entirely nonlethal apprehension tool. Exceptionally useful for nonlethal close-quarters battle.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with identification modification programs.
This poster seems to be instill that a 'Head of Security's Office being overtop a syndicate installation is only fitting. As above.. so below.'
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Bluespace technologies on the application of bureaucracy.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
To be issued to those authorized to act as deputy of security.
A box claiming to contain holobadges.
A box full of PDA cartridges used by Security.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images. This one will refuse to auto-connect incoming calls.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A set of Nanotrasen regulations for keeping law, order, and procedure followed within their space stations.
It has some unsavory stains on it...
Blocks of stone arranged in a tile-like pattern, odd, really, how it looks like real stone too, because it is!
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
A rubber stamp for stamping important documents.
A desk lamp with an adjustable mount.
A charging dock for energy based weaponry, PDAs, and other devices.
An immaculately polished gold security badge. Labeled 'Head of Security.'
Heavy duty, airtight, plastic flaps. Definitely can't get past those. No way.
A wooden musical instrument with four strings and a bow. \"The devil went down to space, he was looking for an assistant to grief.\"
Makes all your shredding needs possible.
It's made of wood and has bronze strings.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
Use this button after you've served someone to tell the next person to come forward.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
A warning sign which reads 'NO SMOKING'.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A warning sign which reads 'RADIOACTIVE AREA'.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
A brown roll of tobacco and... well, you're not quite sure. This thing's huge!
A deck of space-grade playing cards.
A special pipe to bridge pipe layers with.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A pump for cycling an external airlock controlled by the connected doors.
A shutter with a thick see-through polycarbonate window.
A Modello 3 Coffeemaker that brews coffee and holds it at the perfect temperature of 176 fahrenheit. Made by Piccionaia Home Appliances.
A coffee cartridge manufactured by Piccionaia Coffee, for use with the Modello 3 system.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A solar panel. Generates electricity when in contact with sunlight.
A silent polaroid camera with extra capacity for crime investigations.
An immaculately polished gold security badge on leather. Labeled 'Detective.'
A chain link fence. Not as effective as a wall, but generally it keeps people out.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A one-way air valve that does not require power. Passes gas when the output pressure is lower than the target pressure.
It's a storage unit for tools.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A small contraption designed to imbue a few drinks with a pleasant chill.
A slab of 100% grass fed award-winning farm meat.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
Oh, so this is a dress-up game now.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
A miniature welder used during emergencies.
This device recharges energy-dependent lifeforms, like cyborgs, ethereals, and MODsuit users.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
It's a storage unit for rad-protective suits.
A combined blastdoor and mass driver control unit.
Used to control a linked teleportation Hub and Station.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.

\"I'll sweeten thy sad grave: thou shalt not lack the flower that's like thy face, pale primrose, nor the azured hare-bell, like thy veins; no, nor the leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander, out-sweeten'd not thy breath.\"
A large structural assembly made out of metal; It requires a layer of iron before it can be considered a wall.
A gun rack for storing guns.

A device invented in 2486 for the great Space Emu War by the confederacy of Australicus, these high-tech boomerangs also work exceptionally well at stunning crewmembers. Just be careful to catch it when thrown!
